answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% spend cut and the incumbent refuses to reopen price, so renewing or negotiating terms with the incumbent will not close the gap. Deferring past a 14-day expiry with the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer is unsafe; c5 showed deferral only works when month-to-month coverage is available and here the contract does not auto-renew. Adding a second source (c3) is the right structural move long-term but takes longer than 14 days to actually move price on the primary line, so it cannot be the ONE action that closes this year's gap. The lowest-risk path to an 18% cut is to switch primary supply to the low-cost vendor. memory_c2 directly supports this: the same vendor move already cut unit cost sharply last year, onboarding was quick, and invoicing stayed accurate. I am pulling c2's source archive to confirm there is no late-cycle information (a price change, a quality issue, a capacity change) that would invalidate using that vendor again at the volumes needed for an 18% reduction. Pending that one verification, the intended action is switch_primary_vendor; downstream value risk is flagged because the line is running near capacity with no buffer and the change must be sequenced to protect delivery.
